questions.tested_concept: Respiratory acidosis from CO₂ retention with renal bicarbonate compensation

questions.visual_target: Integrate the primary clinical data table with the case context to select the only fully concordant conclusion.

Metabolic acidosis with pulmonary CO₂ retention
Respiratory alkalosis with renal bicarbonate generation
Metabolic alkalosis from gastric acid loss
A fully compensated disorder with normal acid-base status
choice_rationales: The primary abnormality is marked CO₂ retention with acidemia; elevated bicarbonate reflects renal compensation, and low pO₂ supports a pulmonary cause.

Metabolic acidosis with pulmonary CO₂ retention does not account for the complete displayed pattern. A high rather than low pCO₂ drives the acidemia, and the bicarbonate direction is compensatory rather than the source of alkalemia.

Respiratory alkalosis with renal bicarbonate generation does not account for the complete displayed pattern. A high rather than low pCO₂ drives the acidemia, and the bicarbonate direction is compensatory rather than the source of alkalemia.

Metabolic alkalosis from gastric acid loss does not account for the complete displayed pattern. A high rather than low pCO₂ drives the acidemia, and the bicarbonate direction is compensatory rather than the source of alkalemia.

A fully compensated disorder with normal acid-base status does not account for the complete displayed pattern. A high rather than low pCO₂ drives the acidemia, and the bicarbonate direction is compensatory rather than the source of alkalemia.
questions.explanation: The primary abnormality is marked CO₂ retention with acidemia; elevated bicarbonate reflects renal compensation, and low pO₂ supports a pulmonary cause.

questions.stem: An ICU patient is receiving mechanical ventilation with an excessive respiratory rate. Which intervention targets the primary disturbance?

options: Increase minute ventilation to eliminate retained CO₂
Reduce ventilator-driven minute ventilation to correct acute respiratory alkalosis
Infuse bicarbonate for primary metabolic acidosis
Give chloride-rich fluid for vomiting-induced alkalosis
Restrict ventilation until pCO₂ exceeds 50 mm Hg
choice_rationales: Increase minute ventilation to eliminate retained CO₂ does not account for the complete displayed pattern. The primary abnormality is excessive CO₂ removal, not CO₂ retention, bicarbonate loss, or gastric acid loss.
Excess mechanical ventilation lowers pCO₂ and raises pH; adjusting the respirator downward addresses the primary acute respiratory alkalosis.

Infuse bicarbonate for primary metabolic acidosis does not account for the complete displayed pattern. The primary abnormality is excessive CO₂ removal, not CO₂ retention, bicarbonate loss, or gastric acid loss.

Give chloride-rich fluid for vomiting-induced alkalosis does not account for the complete displayed pattern. The primary abnormality is excessive CO₂ removal, not CO₂ retention, bicarbonate loss, or gastric acid loss.

Restrict ventilation until pCO₂ exceeds 50 mm Hg does not account for the complete displayed pattern. The primary abnormality is excessive CO₂ removal, not CO₂ retention, bicarbonate loss, or gastric acid loss.
questions.explanation: Excess mechanical ventilation lowers pCO₂ and raises pH; adjusting the respirator downward addresses the primary acute respiratory alkalosis.

Isolated pulmonary CO₂ retention causes respiratory acidosis
Reduced filtration and excretion of fixed acids plus impaired HCO₃⁻ handling cause high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis
Gastric HCl loss causes chloride-responsive metabolic alkalosis
Increased ammonium generation in damaged nephrons causes alkalemia
choice_rationales: Excess distal H⁺ secretion causes normal-gap metabolic alkalosis does not account for the complete displayed pattern. The source identifies broad loss of renal acid-handling capacity, not acid overexcretion, gastric loss, or an isolated lung disorder.

Isolated pulmonary CO₂ retention causes respiratory acidosis does not account for the complete displayed pattern. The source identifies broad loss of renal acid-handling capacity, not acid overexcretion, gastric loss, or an isolated lung disorder.
Advanced nephron loss impairs fixed-acid filtration and H⁺ excretion as well as bicarbonate reclamation and generation, producing metabolic acidosis with retained unmeasured anions.

Gastric HCl loss causes chloride-responsive metabolic alkalosis does not account for the complete displayed pattern. The source identifies broad loss of renal acid-handling capacity, not acid overexcretion, gastric loss, or an isolated lung disorder.

Increased ammonium generation in damaged nephrons causes alkalemia does not account for the complete displayed pattern. The source identifies broad loss of renal acid-handling capacity, not acid overexcretion, gastric loss, or an isolated lung disorder.
questions.explanation: Advanced nephron loss impairs fixed-acid filtration and H⁺ excretion as well as bicarbonate reclamation and generation, producing metabolic acidosis with retained unmeasured anions.

questions.tested_concept: Proximal tubular dysfunction causing Fanconi syndrome with renal tubular acidosis
questions.stem: A child has aminoaciduria, renal glycosuria, and normal serum creatinine. Which lesion unifies the solute losses and acid-base pattern?
questions.visual_target: Integrate the primary clinical data table with the case context to select the only fully concordant conclusion.
options: Advanced glomerular failure with retention of fixed acids
Proximal tubular dysfunction causing Fanconi syndrome with renal tubular acidosis
choice_rationales: Advanced glomerular failure with retention of fixed acids does not account for the complete displayed pattern. The normal creatinine and normal anion gap point away from glomerular failure or ketoacids, while the low bicarbonate excludes vomiting alkalosis.

Vomiting with chloride-responsive metabolic alkalosis does not account for the complete displayed pattern. The normal creatinine and normal anion gap point away from glomerular failure or ketoacids, while the low bicarbonate excludes vomiting alkalosis.

Primary respiratory acidosis from hypoventilation does not account for the complete displayed pattern. The normal creatinine and normal anion gap point away from glomerular failure or ketoacids, while the low bicarbonate excludes vomiting alkalosis.

Normal filtration with glycosuria, aminoaciduria, bicarbonate loss, hyperchloremic normal-gap acidosis, and inappropriately alkaline urine identifies proximal tubular dysfunction and Fanconi-associated RTA.

Diabetic ketoacidosis from insulin deficiency does not account for the complete displayed pattern. The normal creatinine and normal anion gap point away from glomerular failure or ketoacids, while the low bicarbonate excludes vomiting alkalosis.
questions.explanation: Normal filtration with glycosuria, aminoaciduria, bicarbonate loss, hyperchloremic normal-gap acidosis, and inappropriately alkaline urine identifies proximal tubular dysfunction and Fanconi-associated RTA.
visual_clues: Glycosuria and aminoaciduria despite normal creatinine
Normal anion gap with bicarbonate loss

questions.tested_concept: Respiratory alkalosis plus high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis from salicylate toxicity
questions.stem: An 18-year-old takes a massive aspirin overdose and develops deep, rapid breathing. Which mixed disorder accounts for the direction and magnitude of all values?
questions.visual_target: Integrate the primary clinical data table with the case context to select the only fully concordant conclusion.
options: Pure respiratory alkalosis with appropriate bicarbonate compensation
Pure high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis with appropriate hyperventilation
Normal-gap metabolic acidosis plus chronic respiratory acidosis
Respiratory alkalosis plus high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis from salicylate toxicity
choice_rationales: Pure respiratory alkalosis with appropriate bicarbonate compensation does not account for the complete displayed pattern. Bicarbonate is far lower than expected for an isolated respiratory alkalosis, while the very low pCO₂ is too prominent for a lone metabolic acidosis.

Pure high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis with appropriate hyperventilation does not account for the complete displayed pattern. Bicarbonate is far lower than expected for an isolated respiratory alkalosis, while the very low pCO₂ is too prominent for a lone metabolic acidosis.

Metabolic alkalosis plus respiratory acidosis does not account for the complete displayed pattern. Bicarbonate is far lower than expected for an isolated respiratory alkalosis, while the very low pCO₂ is too prominent for a lone metabolic acidosis.

Normal-gap metabolic acidosis plus chronic respiratory acidosis does not account for the complete displayed pattern. Bicarbonate is far lower than expected for an isolated respiratory alkalosis, while the very low pCO₂ is too prominent for a lone metabolic acidosis.
Salicylate stimulates ventilation, sharply lowering pCO₂, while organic-acid generation lowers bicarbonate and raises the anion gap; the alkalemic pH reflects the mixed process.
questions.explanation: Salicylate stimulates ventilation, sharply lowering pCO₂, while organic-acid generation lowers bicarbonate and raises the anion gap; the alkalemic pH reflects the mixed process.
visual_clues: pCO₂ 14 mm Hg indicates strong respiratory alkalosis
HCO₃⁻ 9 mEq/L and gap 27 indicate added metabolic acidosis
